feature: SharedChannel direct ring-to-decoder large identity assembly

reference.pattern: grpc_slice_buffer retains segmented receive ownership and moves slices between transport and byte-buffer boundaries

objective: For known large uncompressed messages, copy directly from the Shared Call ring into the decoder's final exact allocation and skip the temporary max_write_bytes_per_turn chunk without adding Call or Decoder fields.

design.activation: Only an existing identity reassembly or a wrapped ring prefix declaring more than the 64 KiB turn budget uses the direct path.
design.bounded_work: At most max_write_bytes_per_turn bytes move under one State lock acquisition; the reader unlocks between turns so siblings and the endpoint owner can progress.
design.ownership: feedLimitedAssembledOwned transfers the decoder allocation to the consumer on completion; compressed and small/direct messages retain the published path.
design.layout: Shared Call, Decoder, and public event layouts are unchanged.
design.focused_result: 135/135 passed, including wrapped prefix detection, decoder ownership, and 128 KiB slow-reader sibling progress

rejection_reason: The large-message branch was not taken by the zero-byte workload, yet its common read-path check added about 0.129% instructions with 0/8 wins. Roundtrip, p50, and p99 also regressed by 0.23%, 0.24%, and 0.16%; a 256 KiB run was therefore not permitted to override the small-message guard.
follow_up: Do not add large-message detection to every Shared reader turn. Future segmented ownership must be selected below HTTP/2 transport dispatch or through a distinct large-message call implementation whose code is absent from the default zero-byte path.
